author: reek
body: This CANNOT answer the question the stage exists to ask. The model's STATUS.LU does not consult CTRL.ASDE at all, so both arms come back the same here by construction, and that agreement is worth exactly nothing as evidence about the I219. What it does establish is that the stage compiles, that both arms run to completion against a device, that the second arm's bring-up is not wedged by the first, and that the rendered line is well formed. A payload whose stage faults at the bench has spent a trip to discover a compile-time fact.

author: reek
body: "Ran" is asked as "came back carrying a give-up state I recognise", not as "STATUS was nonzero". Those are the same thing only while the bed grants a link: under -e1000-no-link STATUS reads zero on an arm that ran perfectly, and the earlier version of this judge answered no and named itself `both-arms-run` while doing it. A judge whose answer depends on a condition it does not name is the defect this stage already paid for once.

author: reek
body: The second arm must not be poisoned by the first. Both reset and bring the PHY up from scratch, so the later reading has to be as live as the earlier one; a zero here would mean the first arm left the part wedged.

author: reek
body: The arms differ in one bit of CTRL and nothing else, so under a model that ignores ASDE they must agree. If this ever answers no on the EMULATOR, the stage has grown a difference that is not the bit.

author: reek
body: The give-up state is the row that flew and did not paint. Under the model the link comes up, so this reads ok; the arm that matters is the one below, which asks whether a state that is NOT ok can render at all.

author: reek
body: A hand-built arm in each give-up state, so the text for a state this bed cannot produce is still known to render rather than being assumed. The flight that painted nothing is what this arm exists for.
